author: BBC News
description:
More than 360,000 people have been evacuated across France and Spain as unprecedented wildfires continue to spread.

The French President Emmanuel Macron held crisis talks and said his country was facing its most difficult situation since the Second World War. 

Firefighters are still struggling to control the fires, as a new heatwave is forecast to bring further hot, dry conditions that could help fuel the blaze. 

The authorities are warning that a major fire which is now just 9 miles from Bordeaux could continue to burn for months. 

In Spain, more than 60,000 people have been forced to flee their homes near the capital Madrid. 

Fiona Bruce presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Gwyn Loader, Justin Rowlatt and Mark Lowen.

description:
President Donald Trump has paused attacks on Iran for the third night in a row to give diplomacy more time, the US ambassador to the UN said.
 
An Iranian army spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had halted "retaliatory" attacks in the region in response. The pause follows nearly two weeks of daily US strikes and tit-for-tat attacks, effectively unravelling the ceasefire struck in June.
 
Meanwhile, Iran and Oman held several rounds of technical talks in Tehran on Friday and Saturday to discuss management of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei.
 
Elsewhere, Ukraine has dismissed Iranian threats of retaliation, following Kyiv's targeting of an Iranian cargo vessel in the Caspian Sea on Saturday.

author: BBC News
description:
We speak to the BBC's climate editor Justin Rowlatt about the wildfires raging across Europe, and ask him how to prevent these blazes from becoming the new normal. 

More than 300,000 people in France and Spain have fled their homes as the fires continue. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has said the climate emergency is to blame for the fires, and warned that "difficult hours lie ahead" as his country braces for another heatwave. One official said Spain is facing a "national wildfire crisis".

French President Emmanuel Macron has held a crisis meeting in Paris to discuss the government's response as wildfires burn near the city of Bordeaux. The flames there are so intense that they have created their own thunderstorms in the form of pyrocumulonimbus clouds.

author: BBC News
description:
“Cuba’s assault on the United States was never, at root, a quarrel over economic policy or sovereignty or even ownership of a particular territory,” reads the US Department of State’s new report on the communist state 90 miles from the Florida coast. 

“It was a revolution against Western civilization itself”.   

Over the course of 100 pages, Cuba: The Capital of 21st Century Communism draws lines between Cuba and the Black Panthers, the Pan-African movement, radical feminism, Antifa and more.

It concluded that international sympathy for the island’s dire humanitarian crisis overlooks a sinister reality; that, “its power was always ideological, subversive, and parasitic.” 

The Cuban government has dismissed the report as, “a mediocre propaganda pamphlet.”   

How much validity is there to its arguments, and why release it now? 

Michael Bustamante, a professor of history at the University of Miami, joins Asma Khalid from The Global Story podcast to discuss.

description:
What do affordable housing, arsonists, tourism, the Welsh language and council tax have in common? 

The answer... second homes. 

In some parts of Wales, second homes make up nearly a third of all properties. For local young people trying to buy their first home, that raises a big question - are second homes pricing them out of the communities they grew up in? 

In this video, we explore the impact of second-home ownership on housing affordability, local culture and community life in Wales. We hear from residents, experts and policymakers to find out whether second homes are a problem, or whether there are other factors making it harder for young people to get on the housing ladder. 

From economics and housing policy to tourism and the Welsh language, this is a story about far more than property.

Thousands of people gathered for a vigil at the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin, after a vehicle rammed into crowds at the city’s Pride celebration on Saturday night, killing one woman and injuring at least 29 others.
 
On Sunday, the man suspected of carrying out what authorities said was likely an "Islamist terror attack", was shot and killed by police.
 
Officers opened fire when Abdul Ballout, a 21-year-old German citizen with Lebanese heritage, rushed at them with a knife in Spandau, a western borough of Berlin, bringing to an end a massive manhunt that was launched after a white van was driven into a crowd of people near Tiergarten park.

author: BBC News
description:
Andy Burnham has pledged to continue the UK's "unwavering" support for Ukraine ahead of meeting Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday.

The Ukrainian president will become the prime minister's first international visitor since he took office a week ago, which No 10 said "illustrates the strength of the relationship between the two nations".

They will visit a naval base, where Burnham will announce the sharing of the intellectual property behind the UK's new "Stone Cloak" electronic warfare system, enabling Ukraine to produce the technology at scale.

Burnham told the BBC's Laura Kuenssberg ahead of the visit that he was looking forward to it and that his support for Ukraine was "unwavering - it is 100%".
